label: Searches (Statistics Zone)
purpose: Client hotel searches (XML/API availability requests) received by GlobalTravelEngine: number of searches, how many succeeded or failed, hotels requested and returned, and search lead time. The official source for "searches", by customer, destination, guest nationality and travel date.
grain: Search/API requests aggregated per request day, travel day, customer, request type, destination area, guest nationality, channel/interface, availability type and lead-time band.
use_for: number of searches (hotel searches, search requests)
successful and failed searches, search success/failure rate
hotels requested vs hotels returned in searches
searches by customer, market, destination, guest nationality or travel month
how far ahead clients search (search lead time)
not_for: searches before 2026-07-18 (no data here; Statistics History Client has API requests from 2025-10-16)
API calls of all types, response times or look-to-book (Statistics History Client)
B2B web portal traffic (Statistics Client Web)

coverage.note: Continuous daily data only from 2026-07-18 to yesterday; 2025-11 holds one isolated day (2025-11-19). Nothing between 2025-11-20 and 2026-07-17 and nothing for today.

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the client sent the search (the cube's main date).

dates.label: Travel date (check-in searched)
dates.meaning: Check-in date the client searched for; runs up to a year after the request date.

measures.name: [% Hotels Results]
measures.label: Hotel result rate
measures.definition: Hotels returned with availability as a share of hotels requested ([Hotels Results] / [Hotels Requests]).

measures.name: [% Requests KO]
measures.label: Search failure rate
measures.definition: Failed searches as a share of all searches ([Requests KO] / [Total Requests]).
measures.notes: KO most likely includes searches with no availability as well as errors.

measures.name: [% Requests OK]
measures.label: Search success rate
measures.definition: Successful searches as a share of all searches ([Requests OK] / [Total Requests]).

measures.name: [AVG Lead Time (Days)]
measures.label: Average search lead time
measures.definition: Average number of days between the search (request date) and the check-in searched (travel date).

measures.name: [Hotels Requests]
measures.label: Hotels requested
measures.definition: Number of hotels asked for inside searches: a multi-hotel search counts every hotel it asks for (about 5 per search). Not the number of searches.

measures.name: [Hotels Results]
measures.label: Hotels returned
measures.definition: Number of hotels returned with availability in search responses.

measures.name: [Requests KO]
measures.label: Failed searches
measures.definition: Searches answered KO (an error or no availability returned).

measures.name: [Total Requests]
measures.label: Searches
measures.definition: Number of search requests clients sent (OK + KO). 99.7% are Availability requests; the rest are cancellation-policy, booking, cancel and modify requests.
measures.notes: Verified on real data: this, not [Hotels Requests], is the number of searches.

breakdowns.label: Customer
breakdowns.meaning: Client agency or XML partner that sent the searches.

breakdowns.label: Customer code
breakdowns.meaning: Customer code; the same codes as the Bookings cube, so use it to match a customer's searches with its bookings.

breakdowns.label: Market
breakdowns.meaning: Commercial market of the customer.
sample_values: GCC - Except UAE and Local Residence

breakdowns.label: Customer country
breakdowns.meaning: Country of the customer (agency), not of the guests.

breakdowns.label: Integrator
breakdowns.meaning: Technology platform the customer connects through.

breakdowns.label: Master agency
breakdowns.meaning: Parent agency that groups several customer accounts.

breakdowns.label: Agency group
breakdowns.meaning: Commercial group of the customer (region and markup tier).

breakdowns.label: Customer category
breakdowns.meaning: Customer category; almost all traffic is Dubai Link Category.

breakdowns.label: Account manager
breakdowns.meaning: Account manager responsible for the customer.

breakdowns.label: Destination
breakdowns.meaning: Destination searched, at parent-area level (a city, region or country depending on the place).

breakdowns.label: Destination area
breakdowns.meaning: Exact area searched (city or district).

breakdowns.label: Guest nationality
breakdowns.meaning: Nationality of the guests sent in the search.

breakdowns.label: Guest nationality code
breakdowns.meaning: Two-letter ISO code of the guest nationality.

breakdowns.label: Sale channel
breakdowns.meaning: Sales channel of the customer; almost all searches are XML.

breakdowns.label: Interface
breakdowns.meaning: Technical interface the request came through.

breakdowns.label: Request type
breakdowns.meaning: API method; 99.7% of requests are Availability (searches).

breakdowns.label: Search type
breakdowns.meaning: Multi-Hotel (destination search) or One Hotel (single-hotel search).

breakdowns.label: Lead-time band
breakdowns.meaning: Days between the search and the check-in searched, in bands.

breakdowns.label: Lead-time size
breakdowns.meaning: The same bands by name: Small (1-7 days), Medium (8-30), Large (31-90), Very Large (91+).

breakdowns.label: Rate-checker traffic
breakdowns.meaning: Yes when the search came from a third-party rate-checking tool acting for a customer.

breakdowns.label: Rate-checker tool
breakdowns.meaning: Which third-party rate-checking tool sent the search ('Unknown' for normal traffic).

breakdowns.label: Request month
breakdowns.meaning: Month of the request date (M-YYYY).

breakdowns.label: Request week
breakdowns.meaning: Week of the request date, e.g. '41 (2026)'.

breakdowns.label: Request weekday
breakdowns.meaning: Weekday of the request date.

breakdowns.label: Travel month
breakdowns.meaning: Month of the check-in searched (M-YYYY).

named_filters.name: availability searches
named_filters.meaning: Availability (search) requests only; 99.7% of all requests.

named_filters.name: booking requests
named_filters.meaning: Booking requests sent through the API.

named_filters.name: cancellation policy requests
named_filters.meaning: Requests for a hotel option's cancellation policy.

named_filters.name: last-minute searches
named_filters.meaning: Searches for a check-in 1 to 7 days ahead.

named_filters.name: rate-checker traffic
named_filters.meaning: Searches sent by third-party rate-checking tools.

named_filters.name: excluding rate-checker traffic
named_filters.meaning: Normal client searches, without rate-checking tools.

rules: "Searches" (hotel searches, search requests) = [Total Requests]. [Hotels Requests] counts the hotels asked for inside searches (about 5 per search) and must never be reported as the number of searches.
Data is continuous only from 2026-07-18 to yesterday; 2025-11-19 is one isolated day. For any other period before 2026-07-18 say Statistics Zone has no data instead of showing zero.
There is no data for today (loaded daily up to yesterday).
[Requests OK] + [Requests KO] = [Total Requests]. Percentages and [AVG Lead Time (Days)] are ratios: ask the cube at the level needed; never add or average them across rows.
To compare a customer's searches with its bookings, match on 'Customers'[Customer Code] (same codes as the Bookings cube).
'Customers'[Customer Manager] is 'n/a' for most traffic; use 'Customers'[Account Manager].
'Nationalities'[Country] is the guests' nationality; 'Customers'[Country] is the agency's country.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.

review.question: Does "searches" ("hotel searches", "search requests") mean Statistics Zone [Total Requests] (number of search requests) and never [Hotels Requests] (hotels asked for inside those searches)?
review.why: Verified on real data: [Hotels Requests] is about 5x [Total Requests] because each search asks for several hotels, and using it for searches gave wrong answers. 99.7% of [Total Requests] are Availability requests, so it already is the search count.

review.question: Statistics Zone has data only from 2026-07-18 (plus one day in Nov 2025). For searches in earlier periods, should the app say there is no data, or show Statistics History Client [Requests] filtered to request type Availability (from 2025-10-16) as a separately labelled figure?
options: show History Client availability requests, labelled
review.proposed: show History Client availability requests, labelled
review.why: History Client counts the same client API traffic from a different feed (Sep 2026: 5.19 bn requests vs 4.74 bn here, about 9% more), so it answers the question but must not be mixed into one series with Statistics Zone.
